title: Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts Repair-or-Replace Standard
content:
## Authority to authorize

Repair or replacement under a Homeowner Service Contract is authorized only after a covered determination is on file for the service request. Bridgewell, not the customer, chooses between repair and replacement.

## When Bridgewell replaces

Bridgewell replaces the item when any one of these holds; otherwise it repairs:

| Replacement basis | Condition |
|---|---|
| repair cost threshold | the contractor's repair estimate is at or above the tier's repair-to-replace threshold times the replacement cost |
| parts unavailable | the parts needed cannot be obtained within the tier's parts lead time (calendar days) |
| not repairable | the contractor certifies the item cannot be repaired |

*Boundary pair, hypothetical, threshold 0.60, contracted replacement cost 2,000.00:* 0.60 of 2,000.00 is 1,200.00, so a repair estimate of 1,200.00 meets the threshold and the item is replaced; an estimate of 1,199.99 is below it and, absent the other two bases, the item is repaired.

A replacement is a unit of similar features, capacity and efficiency, not of identical brand, color or dimensions, and where current efficiency standards require a different unit the standard-compliant unit is provided. The replacement cost is Bridgewell's contracted replacement cost for a like unit, equipment plus installation.

## Amount paid

> The amount Bridgewell pays on an authorization is the lowest of the cost of the chosen work (the repair estimate for a repair, the replacement cost for a replacement), the remaining item benefit and the remaining aggregate benefit under the benefit cap rules.
>
> **Retirement notice:** this sentence is no longer in force for a replacement authorized after a stalled repair, whose payment is set under the current rule for such replacements. For every other repair or replacement authorization it remains the rule.

When the cost exceeds the amount paid, the customer may pay the difference to the contractor to have the work done, or decline the work. A customer who wants an upgraded model pays the difference between the like unit and the upgraded unit directly to the contractor.

## One open authorization; reversal; completion

Only one repair or replacement authorization is open per service request; a new authorization on the same request requires reversing the earlier one first. An authorization is reversed in full, never in part, when the customer declines the work, when cash in lieu replaces it, or when it duplicated another authorization; a completed authorization is never reversed. The contractor's completion report closes the authorization and starts the repair guarantee or the replacement labor guarantee.

| Reversal reason | Reversal |
|---|---|
| customer declined the work | in full |
| cash in lieu elected | in full |
| duplicate authorization | in full |
| authorization already completed | never reversed |

superseded_clauses: The amount Bridgewell pays on an authorization is the lowest of the cost of the chosen work (repair_estimate for a repair, replacement_cost for a replacement), the remaining item benefit and the remaining aggregate benefit under homeplan_evt_benefit_caps.
